input.content:
1. `app/apps/web/src/features/sessions/AdminSessionRail.tsx` (the `useState` initializer), `routes/_app/admin/index.tsx`, `AllSessions.tsx`, `rail-look.ts`. The rails take `featuredPosition: number | undefined` and `AdminSessionRail` turns it back into an id with `sessions.find((session) => session.position === featuredPosition)?.id` to open the featured card. The route already holds the featured `SessionSummary` (`findFeatured(all)`) and reduces it to a position, then the rail searches the list again for it. The base passed `highlightedId` and needed no search. Cost: a round trip session -> position -> session, and the skeleton call has to pass `sessionExamples[2].position` as well. Fix: pass `featured: SessionSummary | undefined` to the rails; `AdminSessionRail` opens `featured?.id` and calls `railLook(session, featured?.position)`.

2. `app/apps/web/src/routes/_app/index.tsx` (`usePolls({ sessionId: featured?.id ?? "", ... }, { enabled: student && featured != null })`). The empty string stands in for a missing id and is only safe because `enabled` is false in that case. Cost: a placeholder value that the types accept but that is never meant to reach the API. Fix: give the active-polls query for the featured session a small hook that takes `SessionSummary | undefined` and owns the `enabled` guard, or at least keep the guard next to the sentinel in one place.

3. `app/apps/web/src/routes/_app/index.tsx` and `routes/_app/aula.tsx`. Both write `sessions.data == null ? undefined : findFeatured(sessions.data)` (aula then adds `?.id`). `findFeatured` could accept `ReadonlyArray<S> | undefined` and return `undefined` for it, which removes the guard from both routes and lets `useFeaturedSession` keep using it as `select`. Cost: the same null guard repeated at two call sites of a helper introduced by this diff.
